candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel limit types (instream waste-concentration derivations, domestic/irrigation/livestock criteria, acute/chronic aquatic criteria, human health criteria, TMDL need). Which column is treated as the enforceable numeric discharge limit for a given parameter and monitoring period determines whether a reported measurement is compared and which threshold applies.

The acute aquatic instream waste-concentration column is expressed as a formula of effluent concentration rather than a fixed numeric limit. Interpreting whether Ce is a permit effluent limit, a measured value, or an input variable changes the computed acute aquatic threshold and therefore whether measurements exceed the applicable limit.

MQL values define minimum quantitation/reporting levels by pollutant. Interpreting how results reported below MQL, as non-detects, or as missing should be compared against numeric limits affects both whether a compliance comparison is applicable (Purpose A) and how no-result or below-detection evidence is classified (Purpose C).

candidates.locator: Page 27, Section fact_sheet, pollutant row Pentachlorophenol
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row contains a non-blank Ce value (10 ug/l) alongside multiple derived instream criteria and separate numeric criteria columns (e.g., 1, 19, 15, 30 ug/l). Different readings of which cell is operative, or whether Ce itself is the enforceable effluent limit, change the numeric threshold used for compliance comparison.

candidates.locator: Page 27, Section fact_sheet, pollutant row Phenol
candidates.computation_change_reason: The row pairs a Ce value (2.11 ug/l) with much larger domestic and human-health criteria (10500 and 860000 ug/l) and 1E+100 placeholders in several criteria columns. Selecting the operative limit column versus treating some columns as non-operative changes the applicable numeric limit and exceedance determination.

candidates.locator: Page 27, Section fact_sheet, pollutant row Bis(2-ethylhexyl)Phthalate
candidates.computation_change_reason: Like other rows with populated Ce values, this row presents competing numeric candidates (Ce=2.14 ug/l, domestic criteria=6 ug/l, human health=22 ug/l, and derived instream values). Which value is treated as the enforceable discharge limit changes compliance outcomes for reported measurements.

Many criteria cells use the sentinel value 1E+100. Interpreting this as no numeric limit, not applicable, or a literal criterion changes whether numeric compliance comparison is required for those parameters and whether missing or non-detect results should be treated as outside a numeric limit framework.

Ce and Ca are blank while several instream columns read 0 and domestic/human-health criteria are nonzero (70 and 5300 ug/l). Whether blanks mean no effluent limit, zero, or not applicable—and whether the 0 instream values are operative limits—affects both which numeric limit applies and whether comparison is applicable at all.

candidates.locator: Page 27, Section fact_sheet, pollutant row Nonylphenol
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row lacks an MQL value and leaves Ce/Ca blank while still listing acute and chronic aquatic criteria (28 and 6.6 ug/l). Interpreting the missing MQL and blanks affects monitoring/detection obligations (Purpose B), which numeric limits govern comparison (Purpose A), and how absent or below-quantitation results should be classified (Purpose C).

The Need TMDL column is uniformly marked N/A for listed pollutants. Interpreting whether N/A means no TMDL-driven limit applies, TMDL limits are elsewhere, or TMDL status is undetermined can change which enforceable limits are in scope and whether TMDL-related monitoring obligations attach.

The segment groups pollutants under a BASE/NEUTRAL category within a fact-sheet criteria table. Interpreting whether inclusion in this table signals required monitoring for the category or only documents background criteria affects which monitoring obligations are considered applicable for FY2025.
